root_cause.text: RESPONSE packets that encounter temporary failures during decryption are requeued for retry while in a partially decrypted state, allowing them to be processed again with corrupted cryptographic data instead of being discarded and waiting for a fresh packet.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the retry logic that was re-queuing packets on temporary errors (`-ENOMEM` and `-EAGAIN`). The original code in `rxrpc_do_process_connection()` would call `skb_queue_head(&conn->rx_queue, skb)` to requeue the packet when `rxrpc_process_event()` returned a temporary failure, but this occurs after partial decryption has already modified the packet state. The fix unconditionally calls `rxrpc_free_skb(skb, rxrpc_skb_put_conn_work)` to discard the packet instead, relying on the protocol to send another CHALLENGE/RESPONSE exchange rather than attempting to reprocess a partially decrypted packet.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused or obsolete rxrpc_conn_queue_retry_work trace event from the connection event enumeration.
intent_record.what: Removed the line `EM(rxrpc_conn_queue_retry_work, "QUE retry-wk")` from a trace event macro definition in the rxrpc connection event enumeration.
intent_record.how: This removes a trace event entry point for the `rxrpc_conn_queue_retry_work` event. At runtime, this event will no longer be traceable or logged through the kernel's tracing infrastructure, eliminating any instrumentation that was previously capturing when retry work was queued on rxrpc connections.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused variable declaration to clean up code and eliminate compiler warnings.
intent_record.what: Removed the unused variable declaration `int ret;` from the `rxrpc_do_process_connection()` function.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a variable that was declared but never assigned or referenced within the function body. At runtime, this has no functional impact as the variable was not being used; it only reduces memory overhead on the stack frame and removes compiler warnings about unused variables.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify connection event processing by removing retry logic for transient errors, treating all processed events as complete regardless of outcome.
intent_record.what: Removed the switch statement that handled return values from rxrpc_process_event(). The function call result is no longer captured or checked. Removed conditional logic for -ENOMEM and -EAGAIN error cases that would requeue the skb and schedule retry work. Now unconditionally calls rxrpc_free_skb() after every rxrpc_process_event() call.
intent_record.how: Previously, when rxrpc_process_event() returned -ENOMEM or -EAGAIN, the skb would be requeued at the head of rx_queue and retry work would be scheduled. Now all skbs are freed immediately after processing regardless of the processing result. This means transient failures (memory pressure, resource contention) will no longer trigger automatic retries—packets will be dropped instead.

relevance_review.reason: This group only removes an unused trace event from an enumeration. It is a cleanup/refactoring change that does not address the core vulnerability issue of RESPONSE packets being requeued in a partially decrypted state with corrupted cryptographic data. The vulnerability requires changes to packet handling logic, decryption state management, or retry mechanisms—not trace event removal.

The vulnerability requires changes to packet handling logic, decryption retry mechanisms, or state management - not variable cleanup.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by removing retry logic for transient errors during packet processing. The vulnerability stems from RESPONSE packets being requeued in a partially decrypted state when encountering temporary failures. By eliminating retry logic and treating all processed events as complete, this change prevents the problematic requeuing of partially decrypted packets, which is the core issue described in the vulnerability.

    rxrpc: Clean up connection abort
    
    Clean up connection abort, using the connection state_lock to gate access
    to change that state, and use an rxrpc_call_completion value to indicate
    the difference between local and remote aborts as these can be pasted
    directly into the call state.
    
    Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present at lines 366-369. When rxrpc_process_event() returns -ENOMEM or -EAGAIN (temporary failures during decryption), the code requeues the skb back to conn->rx_queue using skb_queue_head() at line 367 without any state reset or validation. This allows a partially decrypted RESPONSE packet to be reprocessed in a corrupted state on retry, rather than being discarded and waiting for a fresh packet. The vulnerability is that the packet retains any partial decryption state from the failed attempt, violating the requirement that failed decryption attempts should result in packet discard rather than requeue-for-retry with corrupted cryptographic data.

When rxrpc_process_event() returns -EAGAIN (temporary failure during decryption), the packet is requeued back to conn->rx_queue via skb_queue_head() at line 367 while in a partially decrypted state.
